sentences.show: In 1554, a princess was locked in the Tower of London. The queen was warned: you will never be safe while she lives.
Four years later, on this day in 1558, that princess became queen. Elizabeth the First.
Her mother, Anne Boleyn, was beheaded before Elizabeth turned three. She was declared illegitimate.
When her half-sister Mary was queen, a rebellion broke out, and Elizabeth was questioned.
She was sent to the Tower, protesting her innocence.
With no hard evidence, Mary spared her.
She spent almost a year under house arrest. Crowds cheered her along the way.
Then Mary died, aged 42, and Elizabeth became queen, at 25.
She ruled for 44 years, and never married.
She saw off the Spanish Armada, and gave her name to an age.
Also on this day: Prague's Velvet Revolution began, and Napoleon won at Arcole.
